# AppearanceControl

`AppearanceControl` lets a person choose Light, Auto or Dark. It reads and updates the nearest `BreezeProvider`, which resolves Auto against the operating system preference.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

The application owns persistence. Save the value reported by `BreezeProvider` and pass it back as `appearance` on the next visit; `AppearanceControl` does not read or write browser storage.

## Theme-reactive shadows

Shadows use CSS variables so they change with the resolved appearance alongside colours and native controls.

<Canvas of={Stories.ThemeReactiveShadow} />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './AttachmentRow.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Shows an attached document or photograph with its visible status and actions."
/>

# AttachmentRow

`AttachmentRow` presents one attached file in a compact row. The caller provides
the file name, whether it is a document or photograph, its size in bytes, and a
visible status such as `Uploaded` or `Upload failed`. Size formatting follows
the required Breeze provider locale.

## Document and photo thumbnails

Documents use a page preview and photographs use the supplied image thumbnail
or a camera placeholder. The file type is also written as visible text, so the
thumbnail is not the only way to tell them apart. Only a photograph accepts a
`thumbnailUrl`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Document} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Photo} />

## Open and menu actions

Pass `onOpen` to show a direct Open button. Pass action descriptors and an
`onAction` callback together to show the overflow menu; `onAction` receives the
selected action from `actions`. Each action has a visible label; icons only
decorate those labels. The Open button keeps its short visible label, and the
overflow menu opens from an icon-only More actions button. Both include the
file name in their accessible names.

The menu opens aligned to the end edge of its button. Give a destructive action, such as
Remove, `tone: 'danger'` and its own `section` so it shows in the danger
colour below a divider.

<Canvas of={Stories.Document} />

## Narrow containers

When there is not enough horizontal room, the row wraps its actions below the
file details so the file information remains readable.

<Canvas of={Stories.NarrowContainer} />

## Visible state and loading

The `status` text stays visible and updates are announced politely regardless
of the file type or thumbnail. While the file details are unavailable, set
`loading` to show the row-shaped loading placeholder and labelled progress bar.
The placeholder row sits on the surface fill rather than the raised fill, so its
skeletons stay visible in the dark appearance.

<Canvas of={Stories.UploadFailed} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## API

files-documentviewer--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './DocumentViewer.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Opens an attached image or document in an accessible full-screen preview."
/>

# DocumentViewer

`DocumentViewer` presents one attachment in a full-screen reading surface with
zoom, rotation, download, and optional app-owned Replace and Remove actions.
The toolbar displays the current zoom percentage beside the zoom controls.
Use it with `AttachmentRow` by passing the same unique `transitionName` to both
components. The viewer owns its dialog and toolbar; the surrounding record owns
attachment meaning, storage, replacement, and removal.
The viewer is controlled: pass both `open` and `onOpenChange`, and let the
owning screen provide the trigger and state.

The viewer is non-modal. Opened from a record sheet, it covers the viewport
without making the sheet inert, and the sheet keeps its scrim; the viewer adds
none. Escape and Close return focus into the sheet, and closing the sheet first
also closes the viewer.

Although the covered content stays in the accessibility tree, keyboard focus is
contained while the viewer is open: Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, and focus
moved into the covered content is returned to it. Page scrolling is locked for
as long as it is open, whether it was opened from a sheet or from a plain page.
ADR 0002 records why the viewer is non-modal and what that trades away.

## Images and PDFs

Images render directly and do not load the PDF engine. PDFs use the optional
`pdfjs-dist` peer dependency to paint each page to a canvas and provide a
selectable text layer. PDF.js and its worker load only after an open PDF is
requested. Install a compatible `pdfjs-dist` version (`^6.2.108`) in the
application to enable this renderer. If PDF.js cannot load or render a file,
the viewer falls back to the browser's PDF frame.

An absent peer is handled at build time by the application's bundler, not by
Breeze UI. Vite replaces the unresolved optional import with a module that
throws when it is loaded, so the viewer reaches its browser-frame fallback.
Other bundlers may instead fail the application build; install `pdfjs-dist`
or mark it as an ignored optional module in that bundler's configuration.

PDF.js downloads each PDF in a single request rather than in byte ranges.
Attachment URLs are presigned for 30 seconds, and a range request made after
that window would fail with a 403 that permanently breaks the open document.

PDFs that use predefined Adobe character maps or PDF.js standard font files
also need those matching directories served by the application. Copy the
`cmaps/` and `standard_fonts/` directories from the installed `pdfjs-dist`
version to public asset paths, then pass their directory URLs to the PDF
viewer:

```tsx
<DocumentViewer
  mediaType="pdf"
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  pdfAssets={{
    cMapUrl: '/pdfjs/cmaps',
    standardFontDataUrl: '/pdfjs/standard_fonts',
  }}
  src={source}
  title="Quarterly report"
/>
```

These URLs must serve the matching files from the same `pdfjs-dist` version.
The viewer adds a trailing slash to each directory URL. The auxiliary assets
are optional when a document does not reference them.
By default the viewer locates the worker with
`new URL('pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.mjs', import.meta.url)`, which Vite 8.1.5
resolves in production builds and emits as an asset. Vite's development server
resolves this default only when Breeze UI is excluded from dependency
pre-bundling:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  optimizeDeps: {
    exclude: ['@motech-development/breeze-ui'],
  },
});
```

Otherwise, or when the application uses a bundler that does not support this
pattern, provide `pdfAssets.workerSrc` with the URL emitted or copied for the
installed `pdfjs-dist` version.

When PDF.js is unavailable or cannot render a file, the viewer fetches the PDF
and passes its bytes to the browser's native PDF viewer as a PDF-typed Blob.
The source must be readable by the application: same-origin files work directly,
and cross-origin hosts must allow CORS. If the fetch fails, the preview reports
that it is unavailable and the Download action remains available.

The reader supports page navigation for multi-page PDFs. Zoom and rotation
apply to images, rendered PDF pages, and browser-owned frames. Each PDF zoom
step re-renders the page at the new density; the previous rendering stays
visible, and the scroll position is kept, until the sharper page replaces it.
Each preview starts closed inside its own frame; use its Open button to view the
attachment. The PDF example loads PDF.js only after you open it.

<Canvas of={Stories.ImageDocs} />

<Canvas of={Stories.PdfWorkerDocs} />

The compact toolbar keeps the filename and document actions in one raised strip.
For multi-page PDFs, page navigation sits in a separate neutral row beneath it.

## AttachmentRow transition

Give the row and viewer the same stable `transitionName` to morph between the
attachment row and the reader in both directions. Close and Escape return to the
row while preserving the surrounding overlay. The loaded image or PDF remains
covered until the opening morph finishes, then its rendered content is revealed.
Unsupported View Transition APIs and reduced-motion preferences use the same
flow without animation.

<Canvas of={Stories.FromAttachmentRowDocs} />

## Accessibility and fallback limits

Rendered PDF canvases do not expose their page content to assistive technology.
PDF text is selectable visually, but document tags, reading order, and scanned
image OCR are not interpreted. The notice in the viewer therefore states that
the attachment's meaning comes from its surrounding record and offers the
original download.

The fallback iframe is browser-owned. Its controls, keyboard behavior, and
accessibility vary by browser and document type; Breeze cannot inspect or
improve the embedded viewer's content. Use `mediaType="document"` for other
browser-renderable formats when embedding is appropriate. These document frames
are sandboxed so embedded HTML or SVG cannot run scripts in the application.

## Bundle measurement

With Breeze UI's development pin `pdfjs-dist@6.3.289`, the measurements on
2026-10-02 show the package and PDF.js engine as separate gzip payloads. The
PDF.js figure sums the independently compressed main-thread and worker files.

| Payload                                                                     |  Gzip size |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------: |
| Breeze UI library JavaScript (package output, including bundled React Aria) | 133.55 KiB |
| PDF.js engine JavaScript (main + worker, independently compressed)          | 634.60 KiB |

## Actions

The Download link is always available. Cross-origin sources are fetched as a
blob so the requested filename is preserved; the file host must allow CORS from
the application. If that request fails — blocked by CORS, or refused because a
presigned URL has expired — the viewer reports that the file could not be
downloaded and stays open. It never navigates the application's tab to the
source. Replace and Remove buttons appear only when
their corresponding callbacks are provided, leaving mutation and confirmation
flows in the application. Full screen appears only when the browser reports
support for the native Fullscreen API.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './FileDropZone.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Accepts files by drag and drop or through an accessible picker button, with visible validation feedback."
/>

# FileDropZone

`FileDropZone` accepts files through drag and drop or the **Choose files**
button. The button opens a native file picker, so keyboard users can browse for
files without dragging. `label` is shown as a field label above the drop area
and names it.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Compact

Set `compact` to lay the drop area out as one row at the height of an
`AttachmentRow`, so a single attachment keeps its position whether or not a file
is attached. Its secondary line stays on one line and truncates with an
ellipsis.

<Canvas of={Stories.Compact} />

## Take photo

Set `camera` to offer **Take photo** before **Choose files**. It opens a native
file input with `accept="image/*"` and `capture="environment"`, so phones open
the rear camera and other devices fall back to an image picker. Cameras deliver
JPEG photos, so the action appears only when `accept` is omitted or allows JPEG
through `image/*`, `image/jpeg`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `*/*`. Captured photos pass
the same type, size and count checks as chosen files and reach `onFilesAdded`
the same way. For JPEG files, `.jpg` and `.jpeg` accept either extension, and
an untyped file named `.jpg` or `.jpeg` counts as `image/jpeg`.

On coarse pointers and below Breeze's `md` breakpoint, Take photo is filled in
the brand colour. Below `md` it also fills the stacked layout's action row, the
stacked layout hides its drag-and-drop line, and the compact layout reduces both
actions to icons that keep their accessible names.

<Canvas of={Stories.TakePhoto} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Phone} />

<Canvas of={Stories.CompactPhone} />

## File limits

Pass `accept` as a comma-separated list of file extensions and MIME types, such
as `.pdf,image/*`. Dropped files are checked against the same rules. Set
`maxSize` in bytes and `maxFiles` for the total attachment limit. When existing
files are already attached, provide their number as `currentFileCount`.

The component shows each rejection reason in visible text and announces the
same message through a polite live region. Supported files are passed to
`onFilesAdded` as a readonly array. The application owns the attachment state,
upload, and storage work.

Picker text, instructions, and feedback use the BreezeProvider `messages`
override boundary. Translations retain the placeholders documented in the
BreezeProvider locale section, and each message announces with its matching
language.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithExistingFiles} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ChooseAFile} />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './StatStrip.stories';

  summary="Presents a few headline currency figures side by side in one panel."
/>

# StatStrip

`StatStrip` presents headline currency figures, such as a balance and the VAT
owed, as labelled cells in one panel. It reads as a named group containing a
description list, so each label is announced with its figure.

<Canvas of={Stories.Overview} />

## Describe each figure

Pass application values through `items` and return a closed
`StatStripItemDescriptor` from `getItem`. Each descriptor has a stable `id`, a
visible `label`, and a `value` with its `currency`. The value is formatted by
`Typography`'s `money` role for the provider locale, with a minus sign for
negative amounts; a non-finite value or a malformed currency code throws a
`RangeError`.

An optional `badge` follows the label to show the figure's scope, such as the
VAT scheme. It takes the same `children`, `variant` and `aria-label` fields as a
collection item's badge.

## Loading

Set `loading` to replace the figures with three skeleton cells shaped like the
labels and figures they stand in for. `items` and `getItem` are optional while
loading.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Phone layout

Below Breeze's medium breakpoint the cells stack in one column, with a divider
above each cell after the first.

<Canvas of={Stories.Phone} />

## API

# StatePanel

`StatePanel` presents application-owned copy for an empty or failed content
state as a labelled section.

The section is not a live region. Applications own any dynamic announcements
needed when content changes.

When `StatePanel` owns the page's primary action, omit that action from the page
header so the page does not show duplicate calls to action.

## Empty states

Provide the title and explanation your application owns. An empty state may omit
an action or offer one primary action.

<Canvas of={Stories.Empty} />

<Canvas of={Stories.EmptyWithAction} />

## Error states

An error recovery action is optional. When supplied, its label and callback are
required together, and activating it must perform the recovery work.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ErrorWithRecovery} />

## Icon

The panel selects a brand document icon for empty states and a danger warning
icon for errors. Set `icon` to another curated Breeze icon when that better
describes the content.

<Canvas of={Stories.CustomIcon} />

## API

actions-button--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Button.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Performs an action or submits a form." />

# Button

Buttons let users perform an action, such as saving a record or submitting a form.

## Basic button

`Button` comes with four variants: `primary` (default), `secondary`, `quiet` and `danger`. The `children` prop sets the visible label.

<Canvas of={Stories.Primary} />

## Secondary button

Secondary buttons are neutral alternatives to the primary action, such as cancelling.

<Canvas of={Stories.Secondary} />

## Quiet button

Quiet buttons are 13px text actions with no border, fill or control height, for actions that sit alongside content, such as Mark all as read in a panel header or Download on a row. They have one size and do not accept `size`. Use a `Link` when the action navigates.

<Canvas of={Stories.Quiet} />

<Canvas of={Stories.RowAction} />

## Danger button

Danger buttons are destructive actions. Use a label that states what will be removed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Danger} />

## Sizes

`size` accepts `sm`, `md` (default) and `lg`, with minimum heights of 32, 36 and 52px. Small labels are 12px and the others 13px, all semibold. Sizes apply to the `primary`, `secondary` and `danger` treatments.

<Canvas of={Stories.TreatmentsAndSizes} />

Labels wrap and increase the height of the button:

<Canvas of={Stories.LongLabel} />

## Icon

`icon` places a Breeze icon 8px before the label, in every variant and size: 15px at `size="sm"`, and 16px at `md` and `lg`. The icon is decorative, so the label remains the accessible name. While loading, the icon is hidden with the label.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithIcon} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the action is in progress. The label is replaced by a skeleton, and the button cannot be activated again.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Disabled

`disabled` prevents activation and removes the button from the tab order.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Handling actions

`onAction` is called when the button is activated, and takes no arguments.

<Canvas of={Stories.Activation} />

## Form submission

Use `type="submit"` to submit the containing form, and handle submission on the form. The default is `type="button"`. The `form`, `name` and `value` props are available for form association.

## Accessibility

The label provides the accessible name and is retained while the button is loading. Buttons receive a 44px minimum target on touch devices. Quiet buttons receive a 44px minimum height instead, on touch devices and below the `md` breakpoint. `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup` are supported.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Calendar.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A six-week, Monday-first calendar with ISO date values."
/>

# Calendar

`Calendar` renders a locale-aware calendar grid. The month heading sits at the
start of the header with the previous and next month controls together at the
end. Weeks begin on Monday, weekday columns use the provider locale's narrow
names, and each month uses six rows. Leading and trailing dates remain visible
in muted text. Selected dates use a brand fill; today uses a brand outline unless
it is selected.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## States

Use `disabled` to prevent date changes.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Controlled values

Provide `value` and `onChange` for controlled usage. The callback receives an
ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string, never a DOM event. Use `defaultValue` and an optional
`onChange` for uncontrolled usage; the two forms cannot be mixed.

## Accessibility

The `label` names the calendar. React Aria provides keyboard navigation,
selection semantics and localized weekday and date names. Each date's accessible
name includes its full weekday, so the narrow column headings are not its only
cue. The selection fill keeps at least 3:1 contrast with the background in both
appearances, so the selected date needs no additional outline.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import * as Stories from './Card.stories';

<Meta

  summary="Decorates related content as a bordered Breeze panel."
/>

# Card

`Card` groups related non-interactive content on a surface with panel elevation. Padding is selected from the Breeze spacing scale.

<Canvas of={Stories.Surface} />

## Raised cards

Use `raised` for a group nested inside another surface, not to create stronger elevation.

<Canvas of={Stories.Raised} />

## Titles

Set `title` to add a header with a second-level heading that also names the card. Add `count` to show a neutral count beside the title.

<Canvas of={Stories.TitledWithCount} />

Use `action` for one trailing header control, such as a link to the full list. Below a title, `padding` applies to the content only, so set it to `0` for rows that run edge to edge.

<Canvas of={Stories.TitledWithAction} />

## Accessibility

Cards do not become interactive. Use `article`, `aside` or `section` only when that semantic grouping is meaningful, and provide a label or `title` where the element creates a region. A titled card is named by its heading and does not accept `aria-label`.

Loading belongs to the content inside the card. Compose loading-capable children or explicit `Skeleton` elements so placeholders match the final content structure.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Checkbox.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A flat labelled checkbox with semantic boolean changes."
/>

# Checkbox

`Checkbox` is a closed, labelled boolean control. Its label, optional
description and optional error are flat props, so applications do not need to
compose checkbox parts or provide an escape hatch.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Supporting text and errors

Use `description` for guidance. It sits under the label, beside the box. A
non-empty `error` marks the checkbox invalid, appears in the same place and is
associated with the native input. There is no separate invalid prop.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

## States

`required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` map to the corresponding accessible input
semantics. A disabled checkbox greys its box and keeps its label legible.
`loading` keeps the checkbox's shape, announces the provider loading message and
prevents selection until it is removed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Required} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled values

Provide both `selected` and `onChange` for controlled usage. The callback
receives the next boolean, never a DOM event. Use `defaultSelected` and an
optional `onChange` for uncontrolled usage; the two forms cannot be mixed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label alone names the native checkbox, even though its supporting
text shares the clickable label. Descriptions and errors are announced through
React Aria's field relationships, and the field exposes its native input through
`ref`.

## API

# Chip

`Chip` is a compact pill-shaped filter. It stays independently selectable when
shown beside other chips, and exposes its state as `aria-pressed`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Pressed state

Use `defaultPressed` for an uncontrolled chip, or `pressed` and `onChange` when
the application owns the state. The callback receives the next pressed value.
Choose one of these state approaches for each chip.

<Canvas of={Stories.Pressed} />

<Canvas of={Stories.FilterRow} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while saving a choice. A skeleton replaces the visible label while
the chip keeps its name and width. Activation resumes when loading clears.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Disabled and touch targets

Set `disabled` to prevent activation. Chips have a 34px minimum height and
expand to a 44px minimum touch target.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the button. `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and
`aria-describedby` support alternate and supplemental names. The button exposes
its pressed state and supports keyboard activation.

forms-combobox--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './ComboBox.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A filterable suggestion field with optional free text."
/>

# ComboBox

`ComboBox` combines text entry with a popover listbox. Suggestions filter while
the user types, and the same closed descriptor contract is used for every item.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Descriptor content

Pass `items` and a `getItem` mapping function. The mapping returns only
`ItemDescriptor` data: `id`, `label`, optional `description`, `icon`, `badge` and
`disabled`. It cannot return JSX, classes, styles or slot props. A content gap is
a deliberate Breeze library change, not an application markup escape hatch.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

## Filtering and free text

Typing filters suggestions by their descriptor labels. Set `allowsCustomValue`
when the field should also accept text that is not one of the suggestions; the
semantic callback then receives either an item, the entered string or `null`.

When a filter matches no suggestion, or `items` is empty, the listbox stays
open with a localized message that repeats the filter text. Free-text fields
close the suggestions instead, because the entered text is already a valid
value.

<Canvas of={Stories.NoMatches} />

<Canvas of={Stories.FreeText} />

## States

`required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` map to the field's accessible semantics. A
non-empty `error` marks the field invalid; there is no separate `invalid` prop.
`loading` preserves the input shape and prevents interaction until the value is
available.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled values

Provide both `value` and `onChange` for controlled usage. The callback receives a
selected item, custom text or `null`, never a DOM event. Use `defaultValue` and
an optional `onChange` for uncontrolled usage; the two forms cannot be mixed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the input, while descriptions and errors are announced
with the field. Keyboard navigation and focus management are built in.

## API

forms-datepicker--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './DatePicker.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A date field, required by default, with an ISO value and localized trigger."
/>

# DatePicker

`DatePicker` opens a calendar from a button showing the selected date in the
provider locale's long form. The calendar glyph stays at the far edge of the
trigger. The value and callback use ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` strings.

When the field is empty, `placeholder` overrides the provider's `selectDate`
message. Without either override, the English fallback is marked `en-GB` for
assistive technology. `loading` replaces the label, trigger and supporting text
with shape-preserving skeletons, announces the provider loading message, and
disables interaction and form submission until loading clears. The selected
value is retained.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Today

The calendar footer offers a Today action, labelled by the provider's `today`
message. It selects the current date, reports it and closes the calendar.

<Canvas of={Stories.TodayAction} />

## States

Use `error` to display validation feedback and `disabled` to prevent interaction.
`readOnly` keeps the trigger focusable and the date in form submission, but the
calendar cannot be opened, so the date cannot change; use it to show a recorded
date in view mode. A disabled date is omitted from form submission. Use
`loading` while the field's date is unavailable; errors are hidden and an open
calendar closes while loading.

Unlike the other fields, whose `required` defaults to `false`, `DatePicker`
defaults to `required`. This is a deliberate exception: the dates Breeze
applications record are non-null, so an empty date is not a state worth
offering. A required date does not provide a clear control.

Set `required={false}` for an optional date. Its calendar then shows a clear
control beside the Today action, labelled by the provider's `clearDate` message, which empties the
field, closes the calendar and reports `null`. The control is unavailable while
the field is empty. An optional `onChange` must accept `null`, and an optional
uncontrolled field may start from a `null` `defaultValue`; TypeScript rejects
either on a required date.

There is no `autoComplete` prop. The trigger is a button, not a text input, so
browser autofill has nothing to fill.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Optional} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled values

Provide both `value` and `onChange` for controlled usage. Set `value` to `null`
for an empty controlled selection. Use `defaultValue` and an optional `onChange`
for uncontrolled usage; the two forms cannot be mixed, whether the date is
required or optional. An uncontrolled date returns to `defaultValue` when its
owning form resets. With a `name`, the selected ISO date is included in form
submission; an empty value submits an empty string. Override the provider's `required`, `clearDate` and `today` messages to
localize the required announcement, the clear control and the Today action.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the trigger, which exposes required and invalid state.
The calendar supports keyboard navigation and localized date names. Coarse-pointer
targets have a minimum 44px width and height.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Dialog.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Opens a modal surface for a focused task." />

# Dialog

Use `Dialog` for a focused task that needs a centred modal surface and temporarily takes priority over the surrounding page. It remains part of Breeze's public component inventory. Render it inside `BreezeProvider`.

## Basic usage

`trigger` supplies the label for the button Breeze renders. `title` supplies the surface's visible heading and accessible name; `children` supplies its content. Breeze also renders an icon close button whose accessible name comes from the provider's messages.

```tsx
<Dialog title="Delivery details" trigger="View delivery details">
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Dialog>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Open state

By default, the component manages its own open state. Set `defaultOpen` to start open, and optionally use `onOpenChange` to observe changes.

To control the surface from application state, supply both `open` and `onOpenChange`. `open` and `defaultOpen` are mutually exclusive.

```tsx
<Dialog
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="Delivery details"
  trigger="View delivery details"
>
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Dialog>
```

## Dismissal

`dismissible` defaults to `true`, allowing Escape and interaction outside the surface to dismiss it. Set it to `false` when those interactions should leave the surface open. The close button remains available.

## Accessibility and motion

Breeze manages focus on opening and restores it on closing. Modal surfaces contain keyboard focus while open. The provider's portal host keeps the surface's locale, direction and scoped styles intact.

Enter and exit motion respects reduced-motion preferences. A closing surface immediately leaves the active stack while its exit animation completes.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Drawer.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Opens a modal surface from the edge of the page." />

# Drawer

Use `Drawer` for a task or supporting content that needs a modal surface at the edge of the page. Render it inside `BreezeProvider`.

## Basic usage

`trigger` supplies the label for the button Breeze renders. `title` supplies the surface's visible heading and accessible name; `children` supplies its content. Breeze also renders an icon close button whose accessible name comes from the provider's messages.

```tsx
<Drawer title="Delivery details" trigger="View delivery details">
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Drawer>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Content and footer

The content scrolls on its own between the heading bar and the footer. Three props fill a footer pinned below it, which renders only when at least one is given:

- `footerStart` places an action at the start, such as Delete on an edit form.
- `footerSummary` shows a short muted line that takes the free width and truncates.
- `footerActions` places the actions at the end, such as Cancel and Save.

```tsx
<Drawer
  footerActions={
    <>
      <Button onAction={close} variant="secondary">
        Cancel
      </Button>
      <Button onAction={save}>Save transaction</Button>
    </>
  }
  footerSummary="Takes £139.00 off the balance now"
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="New transaction"
  trigger="Record transaction"
>
  <TextField label="Name" />
</Drawer>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.RecordTransaction} />

When the footer runs out of room, its actions wrap onto their own line and stay at the end. Below 768px the summary keeps its full text and moves the actions to the next line, truncating only when it is wider than the footer.

<Canvas of={Stories.EditTransaction} />

Below the medium breakpoint the drawer fills the screen and rises from the bottom.

## Open state

By default, the component manages its own open state. Set `defaultOpen` to start open, and optionally use `onOpenChange` to observe changes.

To control the surface from application state, supply both `open` and `onOpenChange`. `open` and `defaultOpen` are mutually exclusive.

```tsx
<Drawer
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="Delivery details"
  trigger="View delivery details"
>
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Drawer>
```

## Dismissal

`dismissible` defaults to `true`, allowing Escape and interaction outside the surface to dismiss it. Set it to `false` when those interactions should leave the surface open. The close button remains available.

## Surfaces above a sheet

A `Popover` can open above the drawer without blocking interaction with the sheet or hiding its content from assistive technology. The drawer keeps its scrim, and Escape dismisses the popover before the sheet.

`DocumentViewer` opens a non-modal full-screen surface above the drawer. It covers the sheet while keeping it mounted and preserving its scrim. Because the surface is not modal, the covered sheet stays available to assistive technology, while Tab and Shift+Tab stay inside the full-screen surface. Escape closes the full-screen surface before the sheet and restores focus to its opener in the sheet.

The `Foundations/Overlay stack` stories cover sheet/popover and sheet/full-screen compositions, including closing the outer sheet first and starting with nested surfaces open.

## Accessibility and motion

Breeze manages focus on opening and restores it on closing. Modal surfaces contain keyboard focus while open. The provider's portal host keeps the surface's locale, direction and scoped styles intact.

Enter and exit motion respects reduced-motion preferences. A closing surface immediately leaves the active stack while its exit animation completes.

# Grid

`Grid` provides one, two or three equal columns, or a main column beside an aside, on the Breeze spacing scale. Multi-column grids collapse to one column below `md` by default.

<Canvas of={Stories.Responsive} />

## Fixed columns

Set `collapseBelow="none"` only for content that remains understandable at narrow widths.

<Canvas of={Stories.Fixed} />

## Main and aside

Set `columns="mainAside"` for a page with a primary column and a supporting aside, such as the Overview page. Pass exactly two children: the main content first, then the aside. The main column grows to fill the available space beside a 300px aside. Each column keeps its own height, so a short aside does not stretch to match the main column.

Below `md`, the aside stacks under the main content. `collapseBelow` applies as it does to equal columns.

<Canvas of={Stories.MainAside} />

## Accessibility

Grid changes visual arrangement, not reading order. Author children in the order they should be read.

Loading belongs to the items inside the grid. Compose loading-capable children or explicit `Skeleton` elements so each placeholder matches its final item.

| `3xl` | 24     | Large icon buttons, such as the raised action               |

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './IconButton.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Performs an action from an icon alone." />

# IconButton

Icon buttons perform an action, such as closing a panel or opening more actions, where an icon alone is clear enough.

## Basic icon button

`name` selects the artwork from the curated Breeze icon set, and `label` gives the action its accessible name. `label` is required, because the button has no visible text.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Treatments and sizes

`variant` accepts the same treatments as `Button`: `secondary` (default), `primary`, `quiet` and `danger`. The default is `secondary`, because most icon-only actions, such as Close and More actions, sit beside content rather than leading it.

`size` accepts `sm`, `md` (default) and `lg`. The button is square at 32, 36 or 52px, and its icon is 16, 20 or 24px.

<Canvas of={Stories.TreatmentsAndSizes} />

## Shapes

`shape` accepts `square` (default), with the control's rounded corners, and `circle`, for a standalone action such as the application shell's centre action.

<Canvas of={Stories.Shapes} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the action is in progress. The icon is replaced by a skeleton, and the button cannot be activated again.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Disabled

`disabled` prevents activation and removes the button from the tab order.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Handling actions

`onAction` is called when the button is activated, and takes no arguments.

<Canvas of={Stories.Activation} />

## Accessibility

The `label` is the accessible name and is retained while the button is loading. The icon is hidden from assistive technology. Icon buttons receive a 44px minimum target on touch devices, and `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup` are supported.

## API

<ArgTypes />

navigation-link--docs.content: import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import * as Stories from './Link.stories'; # Link `Link` renders a native anchor as a standalone 13px text action without an underline, such as View all money in a panel header. Its `href` remains the destination, so browser navigation, keyboard access and open-in-new-tab behavior continue to work. Use a quiet `Button` for an action that does not navigate. Without a configured router, activating the link uses the browser's native navigation. With a router, Breeze intercepts only qualifying same-document navigations. ## Router navigation Pass a same-document router to `BreezeProvider` when links should update application state without loading another document. `Link` sends the destination and its optional `transitionTypes` to the router. The router decides whether and when to use a browser view transition; see Motion. ```tsx Transactions ``` `transitionTypes` defaults to an empty list. Breeze passes the option to `router.navigate(href, { transitionTypes })`; an existing one-argument `navigate(href)` adapter can ignore the extra argument. The router receives the destination the browser would navigate to, as a root-relative path with its query string, rather than the raw `href`. A relative `href` such as `accounts`, `../reports` or `?page=2` is resolved against the current document first, so `/accounts/transactions/` with `href="?page=2"` routes to `/accounts/transactions/?page=2`. Because the path is root-relative, it already includes any base path the application is served under. **An adapter for a router that prepends its own `basename` must strip that base before navigating**, or the base will appear twice. ## Native anchor behavior The router handles only an unmodified primary click on a same-origin HTTP or HTTPS link with no fragment, download, or alternate browsing target. External links, downloads, alternate targets, modified clicks and fragment links keep the browser's native behavior. Use `variant="subtle"` for a lower-emphasis link. The default variant uses the Breeze brand text colour. ## Accessibility Links are distinguished by colour alone, so place them apart from running text rather than inside a sentence. They receive a 44px minimum height on touch devices and below the `md` breakpoint. The link's visible content is its accessible name by default. Use `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` when that content does not describe the destination, and `aria-current` when the link represents the current page or location. ## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Menu.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="A compact list of actions opened from a button." />

# Menu

`Menu` keeps related actions together under a labelled button. Use it for
secondary actions, such as account settings, that should stay out of the main
page until needed.

When the visible trigger label is shared by several controls, set
`triggerAriaLabel` to give each button a distinct accessible name while keeping
the visible label concise.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Icon-only trigger

Omit `trigger` and set `triggerIcon` and `triggerAriaLabel` together for a
compact icon-only trigger, such as a More actions button. `triggerAriaLabel`
is then required, because it is the trigger's only name.

<Canvas of={Stories.IconOnlyTrigger} />

## Loading the menu

Use `loading` when the trigger should wait before opening. It shows a loading
bar while keeping its size and accessible label; an icon-only trigger replaces
its icon with a skeleton, as `IconButton` does. Actions in an already-open menu
remain available.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Define actions

Pass your application values in `items`. Use `getItem` to provide each value's
`MenuItemDescriptor`: `id` and `label` are required, while `description`,
`icon` or `initials`, `badge`, `disabled`, `section` and `tone` are optional. Give each item a unique `id` within the
menu. Keep labels concise; use descriptions for a short explanation and icons
when they help people scan the choices. When any item has an icon or initials,
every label lines up: items without either keep that space, and in a menu with
initials, icons centre in the tile's width. A menu without either starts its
labels at the edge.

## Destructive actions

Set `tone: 'danger'` on an action that removes or discards something, such as
Remove, to show it in the danger colour. Place it last, in its own `section`,
so a divider separates it from the other actions. The action runs when
selected; confirm its result in the page, as with any other action.

<Canvas of={Stories.DestructiveAction} />

## Group actions into sections

Give items a `section` to group them. Items sharing a section `id` are shown
together where the first of them appears, and dividers separate each section
from its neighbours. A section `label` shows as a header and names the group
for assistive technology; omit it to separate the items with dividers alone,
without a header or a group.

Set `initials` instead of `icon` to show a short code, such as a company's
initials, in a brand tile before the label. The tile is decorative, so the label
must still identify the item.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sections} />

## Menu width

The open menu fits its items and is never narrower than its trigger. `width`
sets its minimum width: `md`, the default, is 256px and suits a list of names
such as a company switcher; `sm` is 208px and suits a short list of actions,
such as the file actions in `AttachmentRow`.

<Canvas of={Stories.NarrowWidth} />

## Placement

The menu opens below its trigger with their start edges aligned. Set
`placement` to `bottom end` to align their end edges instead, for a trigger at
the end of a row. Start and end follow the provider's text direction, and the
menu can adjust its position to fit the available space.

## Panels that are not menus

A menu contains only actions, optionally grouped into labelled sections. Do not
use `Menu` for a panel that also shows information people read but cannot act
on, places controls inside a row or header, or offers a toggle group. Assistive
technology presents a menu as its menu items alone, so plain-text rows are
skipped, and the menu's arrow keys cannot reach a button placed inside an item
or a section header.

An account panel that lists notifications, gives one of them a Download action,
offers Mark all as read and an `AppearanceControl`, and then links to settings
is such a panel. Build it as a `Popover` with application content instead.

## Respond to a selection

`onAction` receives the selected application item from `items`, as
`Select`, `ComboBox` and `ToggleGroup` do. The menu closes when an action is
selected. Show that action's progress, confirmation or errors in
the page or dialog that follows.

Use `defaultOpen` when the menu manages its own visibility. To control
visibility, provide `open` and `onOpenChange` together.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Keyboard use

Open the menu with the trigger button, Enter, Space or ArrowDown. Use the arrow
keys to move through enabled actions; type a label to jump to a matching action.
Enter or Space selects the focused action. Escape closes the menu and returns
focus to its trigger.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './NumberField.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Locale-aware numeric entry with semantic number changes."
/>

# NumberField

`NumberField` is a flat labelled numeric input backed by React Aria. It uses
the Breeze locale and displays figures with tabular numerals. There are no
stepper buttons: the Up and Down arrow keys change the value by `step`. Values
remain unformatted except for React Aria's locale-aware input behaviour.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Sizes

`size` defaults to `md`, the standard 38px control with 13px figures. Use `lg`
for a form's primary amount: a 52px control with 20px semibold figures. Fields
that share a row should share a size.

<Canvas of={Stories.Large} />

## Supporting text and errors

Use `description` for guidance. A non-empty `error` marks the field invalid and
associates the message with the native input. There is no separate invalid prop.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

## States

`required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` map to the corresponding accessible input
semantics. `loading` keeps the field's shape, announces the provider loading
message and prevents typing or stepping until it is removed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Required} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

<Canvas of={Stories.LargeLoading} />

## Controlled values

Provide both `value` and `onChange` for controlled usage. The callback receives
the next number, never a DOM event. React Aria reports `NaN` while the input is
empty, which lets applications distinguish an empty value from zero. Use
`defaultValue` and an optional `onChange` for uncontrolled usage; the two forms
cannot be mixed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the native input. Descriptions and errors are announced
through React Aria's field relationships, and the field exposes its native
input through `ref`.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Popover.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Opens contextual content beside its trigger." />

# Popover

Use `Popover` for non-modal contextual content anchored to a trigger. The surrounding surface remains interactive and available to assistive technology; the popover has no dimmed scrim. Render it inside `BreezeProvider`.

Choose `Popover` rather than `Menu` when the content mixes information with controls, such as a list of notifications with their own actions beside an `AppearanceControl`. A `Menu` holds only a list of actions.

## Basic usage

`trigger` supplies the label for the button Breeze renders. `title` supplies the surface's visible heading and accessible name; `children` supplies its content. Breeze also renders a close button with a label from the provider's messages.

```tsx
<Popover title="Delivery details" trigger="View delivery details">
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Popover>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Open state

By default, the component manages its own open state. Set `defaultOpen` to start open, and optionally use `onOpenChange` to observe changes.

To control the surface from application state, supply both `open` and `onOpenChange`. `open` and `defaultOpen` are mutually exclusive.

```tsx
<Popover
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  open={open}
  title="Delivery details"
  trigger="View delivery details"
>
  <Typography>Your delivery details appear here.</Typography>
</Popover>
```

## Dismissal

`dismissible` defaults to `true`, allowing Escape and interaction outside the surface to dismiss it. Set it to `false` when those interactions should leave the surface open. The close button remains available, so a `panel` cannot set it to `false`.

## Placement

`placement` accepts `top`, `bottom` (default), `start`, `end` or `bottom end`. `bottom end` opens below the trigger with their end edges aligned, for a trigger at the end of a bar. Start and end follow the provider's text direction. The surface can adjust its position to fit the available space.

## Panels

Set `variant` to `panel` for content that names its own purpose, such as an account panel of notifications and settings. A panel shows no title or close button; `title` still names it for assistive technology. Its content runs edge to edge with no padding, and it fits that content from a minimum of 336px, or spans the viewport less 12px on each side on narrow screens. A panel closes with Escape or a press outside it, so it cannot set `dismissible` to `false`.

Set `triggerInitials` to open the popover from a circular button showing a person's initials. `trigger` then supplies only the button's accessible name, so describe what it opens. Set `triggerIndicator` to add an attention dot, such as for unread notifications. Breeze describes the dot to assistive technology with the provider's unread-items message; the dot itself is decorative. Applications that know the count can include it in `trigger`, for example "Account and notifications, 2 unread".

```tsx
<Popover
  placement="bottom end"
  title="Account and notifications"
  trigger="Account and notifications, 2 unread"
  triggerIndicator
  triggerInitials="MG"
  variant="panel"
>
  {/* Notifications, AppearanceControl and account links */}
</Popover>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.AccountPanel} />

## Accessibility and motion

Breeze manages focus on opening and restores it on closing without trapping focus inside the popover. The provider's portal host keeps the surface's locale, direction and scoped styles intact.

Inside a drawer, a popover appears above the sheet while its content remains interactive and accessible. The sheet keeps its scrim. Escape closes the popover first and restores focus to its trigger; a subsequent Escape closes the sheet. The `Foundations/Overlay stack` stories exercise this composition.

Enter and exit motion respects reduced-motion preferences. A closing surface immediately leaves the active stack while its exit animation completes.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './RowList.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A keyboard-accessible list of aligned, actionable rows."
/>

# RowList

`RowList` displays data as actionable rows with aligned leading, metadata and
trailing regions. It uses grid-list semantics and has no column headers.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Describe each row

Pass application values through `items` and return a closed
`RowListItemDescriptor` from `getItem`. Each descriptor has a stable `id` and a
visible `label`. It may also include a `description`, `icon`, `badge`, or
`disabled` state. `metadata` accepts text or an ISO calendar date. `value`
accepts text or a currency amount, formatted with the provider locale. A
currency `value` is passed to `Typography`, so a non-finite amount or a
malformed currency code throws a `RangeError` when the row displays its value.

Use the optional `section` object to group rows under structural section
headers. Keep each section ID stable when rows are appended or merged. Keep row
IDs unique and stable so the focused row remains mounted as data changes.

`metadataAmount` adds a second, muted currency cell, such as VAT, between the
metadata and the value. It formats like a currency `value` without a tone.
Each metadata column and the value column is reserved only when at least one
row in the list uses it; otherwise the leading region extends into that space.

## Summarise a section

Set the section's optional `summary` to end its header with trailing content,
read from the first row in each section. A currency summary takes the same
fields as a currency `value`, shown at the header's 12px size, plus a `label`
that is visually hidden and read before the amount, such as “Confirmed daily
total”. Breeze does not add the amounts up; pass the total with its `tone` and
`sign`. A text summary shows a muted note instead, such as “Not in the balance
yet” for a section that has no total.

<Canvas of={Stories.Money} />

## Phone layout

Below Breeze's medium breakpoint the value stays at the end of the row, the
metadata columns are hidden, and a row's badge moves under its description so
the label keeps the full width. Keep anything essential in the label,
description or value.

<Canvas of={Stories.Phone} />

## Show money in and out

Currency values use the compact `amount` role in the default ink tone. Set
`tone: 'positive'` on money in and `sign: 'always'` to show an explicit `+` or
true minus; `sign` follows `Typography`. Set the row's `direction` to `in` or
`out` to give its icon tile the positive or strong wash, and pair it with the
`incoming` or `outgoing` icon. Without `direction` the tile is neutral. Colour
is never the only signal: the sign and icon also carry the direction.

<Canvas of={Stories.Activity} />

## Activate rows

`onAction` receives the activated row's application item from `items`, as
`Select`, `ComboBox` and `ToggleGroup` do. React Aria supplies the
grid-list keyboard interaction; use the arrow keys to move between rows and
Enter or Space to activate the focused row.

<Canvas of={Stories.Merging} />

## Loading and empty results

Set the top-level `loading` flag while fetching initial data or refreshing. An
empty grid shows three quiet skeleton rows and one loading announcement. A
populated grid keeps its rows and focus while loading, with the announcement
outside the grid.

<Canvas of={Stories.InitialLoading} />

<Canvas of={Stories.RetainedLoading} />

Completed empty results display the provider-localized “No items to display.”
message inside the structural grid row and cell. The single persistent polite
status announces the same message.

<Canvas of={Stories.Empty} />

`RowListItemDescriptor.loading` only replaces a row's optional metadata and
value with quiet placeholders; its label, description, icon, badge, and action
remain. The Loading example shows this state alongside a separately busy named
pagination button.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

Pass a named `loadMore` action when another page is available. Its button keeps
its label while busy, and its status shares the single live loading message
without re-announcing existing rows.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Select.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="A fixed-choice field with a popover listbox." />

# Select

`Select` is a fixed-choice field. Its visible control opens a popover listbox
and participates in browser forms and autofill.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Descriptor content

Pass `items` and a `getItem` mapping function. The mapping returns the closed
`ItemDescriptor` data contract: `id`, `label`, optional `description`, `icon`,
`badge` and `disabled`. It cannot return JSX, classes, styles or slot props.
If an item needs content outside that contract, extend Breeze deliberately rather
than reopening a markup escape hatch.

<Canvas of={Stories.Description} />

The trigger shows the selected item's label and, when the descriptor has one,
its badge at the end of the control. The badge is part of the announced value,
as it is for the option.

<Canvas of={Stories.SelectedBadge} />

## States

`required`, `disabled` and `readOnly` map to the field's accessible semantics. A
non-empty `error` marks the field invalid; there is no separate `invalid` prop.
`loading` preserves the control shape and prevents interaction until the value
is available.

<Canvas of={Stories.Error} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ReadOnly} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Controlled values

Provide both `value` and `onChange` for controlled usage. The callback receives
the selected item or `null`, never a DOM event. Use `defaultValue` and an
optional `onChange` for uncontrolled usage; the two forms cannot be mixed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the control, while descriptions and errors are announced
with the field. Keyboard navigation and focus management are built in.

# Skeleton

`Skeleton` represents content while it loads. Unlike layout primitives, its block and inline dimensions deliberately accept arbitrary CSS lengths so it can match the content it replaces.

<Canvas of={Stories.Shapes} />

## Backgrounds

Skeletons use the sunken fill, as the design does. Place them on surface or canvas backgrounds: in the dark appearance the sunken and raised fills are the same colour, so a skeleton on a raised background disappears.

Supply `label` when the skeleton owns the loading announcement. Omit it when a parent component already announces loading; the skeleton is then hidden from assistive technology.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Toggle.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A binary choice with an accessible pressed state."
/>

# Toggle

`Toggle` represents an on/off choice as a button. Its pressed state is exposed
with `aria-pressed`. Use a `Checkbox` when the choice belongs in a form.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Pressed state

Use `defaultPressed` for an uncontrolled toggle, or `pressed` and `onChange` when
the application owns the state. The callback receives the next pressed value.
Choose one of these state approaches for each toggle.

<Canvas of={Stories.Pressed} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while saving a choice. A skeleton replaces the visible label while
the button keeps its name and width. Activation resumes when loading clears.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Sizes and disabled state

`size` accepts `sm`, `md` (default) or `lg`, with minimum heights of 34, 38 and
52px. Touch targets are at least 44px. Disabled toggles cannot be
activated.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Accessibility

The visible label names the button. `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and
`aria-describedby` support alternate and supplemental names. The button exposes
its pressed state and supports keyboard activation.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './ToggleGroup.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="A single-choice segmented control with accessible pressed options."
/>

# ToggleGroup

`ToggleGroup` presents a single choice as connected segments. Each option is a
button with an accessible pressed state. Press the selected option again to
clear the selection.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Options

Provide `items` and a `getItem` function that describes each option. Return a
unique `id` and visible `label`. You can also provide a `description`, `icon`,
`badge` or `disabled` flag. Disabled options cannot be selected.

<Canvas of={Stories.DisabledOption} />

## Controlled selection

Use `defaultSelected` with an optional `onChange` for uncontrolled use. Provide
`selected` and `onChange` when the application owns state. The callback receives
the selected item, or `null` when the choice is cleared. Choose one of these
state approaches for each group.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while saving a selection. A slim loading bar replaces each
option's content while its size and selected appearance stay in place. Changes
resume when loading clears.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Full width

Set `fullWidth` to stretch the group across its container and share the width
equally between options, for example when the choice sits in a form.

<Canvas of={Stories.FullWidth} />

## Sizes and accessibility

`size` accepts `sm` (default), `md` or `lg`, giving the group a minimum height
of 34, 38 or 52px to align with other controls of the same size. On coarse
pointers every option is at least 44px tall to meet the touch-target minimum, so
the `sm` and `md` groups grow to 50px. Give each group an `aria-label`; each
option exposes whether it is pressed and supports keyboard interaction.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

## API

content-typography--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Typography.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Applies Breeze text roles and locale-aware formatting."
/>

# Typography

`Typography` provides the money, amount, heading, title, body, caption, label and micro roles. Money uses negative tracking and tabular numerals. Set `numeric` on other figure text; interface text retains normal tracking.

<Canvas of={Stories.Roles} />

## Numeric figures

Set `numeric` on figures outside the money role. They gain tabular numerals, negative tracking and logical end alignment without tightening interface headings.

<Canvas of={Stories.FiguresAndInterfaceText} />

## Money and dates

Pass semantic values with `format="currency"` or `format="date"`. Currency uses the `money` role for stat figures or the `amount` role, a semibold body-size figure, for row amounts. Dates use the exported `IsoCalendarDate` string contract. Formatting uses the nearest `BreezeProvider` locale. Currency signs retain that locale's placement and use a true minus character.

<Canvas of={Stories.Formatting} />

By default, `sign="auto"` signs negative amounts only. `sign="always"` also signs positive amounts, and `sign="never"` omits the sign for content that conveys direction another way. Zero is never signed, including negative zero and amounts that round to zero, so `-0.004` displays as `£0.00`.

Calendar dates are formatted in UTC, so the displayed day never shifts. The provider's `timeZone` governs times of day and is not applied to calendar dates.

### Invalid values

An invalid money value is a programming error, so `Typography` throws a `RangeError` that names it instead of displaying a misleading figure:

- `currency` must be a well-formed three-letter code, such as `GBP`. Codes are
  not checked against ISO 4217, so an unknown well-formed code is displayed as
  written.
- `value` must be a finite number. `NaN` and `Infinity` are rejected.
- An invalid `locale` is rejected by `BreezeProvider` before any value is formatted, so it is never reported as a currency error.

Validate or convert untrusted amounts before rendering them. A calendar-invalid date, such as `2026-02-30`, is displayed unchanged.

No separate formatting components are exported.

## Accessibility

Choose the `element` for document semantics; the visual role does not force a heading level. Do not use colour alone to communicate direction or status.

## Loading

Set `loading` to preserve the text's place while its value is unavailable.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## API

<ArgTypes />

foundations-breezeprovider--docs.content: import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import * as Stories from './BreezeProvider.stories'; # BreezeProvider `BreezeProvider` provides the locale, appearance and styles that Breeze UI components require. Render it once, above every Breeze UI component. Components rendered without a provider throw an error. ```tsx ``` ## Locale `locale` takes a BCP 47 language tag. It sets the `lang` attribute and the text direction of the provider's root element. Only English (`en-GB`) messages are bundled. Supply partial `messages` to translate Breeze's loading and required announcements, the DatePicker placeholder and Today action, the ComboBox no-match message, appearance control, overlay close button, Popover unread indicator, FileDropZone instructions and feedback, and attachment labels and actions into the provider locale. Without an override, Breeze's own text uses English and is marked `lang="en-GB"`, independently of the surrounding content's language. Built-in interaction labels are available in English only. `locale` still sets the provider language and direction and formats locale-aware values; use `messages` for the Breeze-owned strings listed above. ```tsx ``` Keep `{query}` in `comboBoxNoMatches`; it is replaced with the filter text. FileDropZone message strings use flat keys. Keep their placeholders when providing translations: `{types}` for accepted types, `{size}` for the size limit, `{count}` for multiple added files, `{current}` and `{max}` for the attachment count, `{fileName}` for a rejected file, and `{fileNames}` for files rejected by the total count limit. For example: ```tsx ``` ## Time zone `timeZone` takes an IANA time-zone name, such as `Europe/London`, reserved for formatting times of day. **No component formats a time of day yet, so today it has no visible effect**; it is validated and provided now so the API does not change when one does. Without it, times of day will use the runtime's time zone. The provider throws a `RangeError` for a name the runtime does not recognise. ```tsx ``` `timeZone` is intentionally not applied to calendar dates. A calendar date, such as `Typography`'s `format="date"`, names a day rather than an instant, so Breeze formats it in UTC and the displayed day never shifts. Applying a western zone to a UTC-midnight date would display the previous day. ## Appearance Appearance defaults to `automatic`, which follows the operating system and keeps following it when the preference changes. The provider resolves the choice to `light` or `dark`, then applies that value and the matching `color-scheme` to the document element. Use `defaultAppearance` when Breeze should hold the current choice in memory: ```tsx saveAppearance(appearance)} > ``` Use `appearance` with `onAppearanceChange` when application state controls it. `appearance` and `defaultAppearance` are mutually exclusive. ```tsx ``` The provider never reads or writes durable browser storage. The application decides whether and where to persist the reported choice. If a persisted explicit choice must apply before the application starts, stamp its resolved value on the document element before loading the stylesheet; the stylesheet's media-query default already handles automatic dark mode before script runs. ## Overlay portal `Dialog`, `Drawer` and `Popover` render into a dedicated portal host owned by the provider. By default, the host is appended to `document.body`. Set `portalContainer` to an existing light DOM `HTMLElement` in the current runtime document when overlays need to render in another container, such as an embedded application or a test fixture. ```tsx ``` The provider creates and removes its own host inside that container. The host carries the Breeze root marker, locale and text direction so overlays retain scoped styling and language outside the provider's normal content tree. `portalContainer` and every overlay trigger must belong to the current runtime `Document` and its light DOM. Cross-document and shadow-root portals are unsupported. ## Client-side navigation Set `router` when the application has a same-document router. `Link` sends qualifying same-origin link activations to `router.navigate`, together with the link's `transitionTypes`. The router owns the route update and can opt into browser view transitions; see Motion. ```tsx ``` The `transitionTypes` option defaults to an empty list. A `navigate` function that accepts only `href` can ignore the second argument. External destinations, downloads, alternate targets, modified clicks and fragment links retain native anchor behavior. ## Confirmations Use `useToast` below the provider to announce a completed action. The provider owns the status region, displays up to three messages at once and queues additional messages in FIFO order. Each message remains visible for 2.6 seconds after it becomes visible. ```tsx import { useToast } from '@motech-development/breeze-ui'; function SaveAction() { const enqueue = useToast(); return ; } ``` Set `toastLimit` when the application needs a different number of visible confirmations. Provider-enqueued confirmations stay 288px wide at every supported viewport, have no action or dismissal control, and expire after 2.6 seconds once visible. ## API
